extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism evidence from Results sections 2.5-2.7, Figures 4-6, and methods 4.6-4.8. Claims are limited to CM5 growth inhibition, time-kill phenotype, and membrane permeabilization evidence; no unsupported molecular target is asserted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CM5 inhibits growth of A. baumannii ATCC19606 and clinical isolates in a concentration-dependent MIC-multiple growth-curve assay.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:2.5. Growth Inhibitory Effects of CM5

mechanism_claims.limitations: Growth curves support inhibitory phenotype, not a standalone molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CM5 shows fast bactericidal activity against A. baumannii ATCC19606 in a concentration-dependent time-killing assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Time-kill kinetics demonstrate bactericidal phenotype but do not identify a molecular receptor.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CM5 causes dose-dependent bacterial membrane permeabilization in A. baumannii ATCC19606, supporting a membrane-lytic action model.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:2.7. CM5 Induces Dose-Dependent Membrane Disruptions of the Bacterial Cells

mechanism_claims.limitations: The article supports membrane permeabilization/lytic model; exact pore architecture is not directly resolved.
